trust_decision.summary: The incremental parser treats a non-self-delimiting top-level token (number/true/false/null) as complete as soon as the scanner hits end of buffer, so the decoded value depends on chunk boundaries; the fix decides in the incr_parse XSUB, before decode_json, that such a token is only accepted when allow_nonref was set explicitly (new F_NONREF_SET recorded by the flag setter).

landing_point.why: The summary names incr_parse and top-level numbers; the XSUB incr_parse and its scanner XS.xs:5169 are the obvious first stop, and the fix lands in the XSUB just before decode_json at XS.xs:5731.

fix_sites.entry_point: Cpanel::JSON::XS->new->incr_parse($text) in scalar or list context (public OO API)
Cpanel::JSON::XS->new->allow_nonref([$enable]) (ALIAS of the generic flag setter, XS.xs:5468)
fix_sites.module_kind: core XS option setter (records explicit-set state)

fix_sites.entry_point: n/a: new flag bit F_NONREF_SET in the flags word, inserted after XS.xs:385

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: No second implementation: the only source files are XS.xs/XS.pm/XS/Type.pm/XS/Boolean.pm; XS.pm has no incr code (only docs, XS.pm:1279-1362), bin/cpanel_json_xs does not call incr_parse, and decode/decode_prefix (XS.xs:5631-5645) are not chunked.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Little to dismiss: the only extra decision is whether allow_nonref is 'explicit'; a solver could argue the default-on F_ALLOW_NONREF (XS.xs:500) already means 'allowed' and leave incr_parse alone, citing the docs that say incr_parse never supported allow_nonref (XS.pm:1352-1362).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Top-level strings (self-delimiting) must still decode incrementally under the default allow_nonref, including mixed with arrays in list context ('"a" [1]'); numbers/true/false/null must still work when allow_nonref is set explicitly; arrays/objects unaffected. A fix that rejects every non-ref (json_nonref after decode, or clearing F_ALLOW_NONREF in incr_parse) breaks strings.

O6_input_shapes: bare number at buffer start, including leading '-' (fix.diff:141)
leading JSON whitespace before the token (fix.diff:134-135)
relaxed '#' comments before the token, only when F_RELAXED (fix.diff:136-139)
second and later values in list context after a previous value was chopped (check sits inside the do/while, fix.diff:161 / XS.xs:5703-5744)
allow_nonref set explicitly vs. left at default vs. explicitly disabled (setter records any explicit call, fix.diff:152-153)

O7_producer.where: The ambiguous end is produced by the incr scanner's nest-0 whitespace/EOF interrupt (XS.xs:5310-5322) and the INCR_DONE macro (XS.xs:450); the check calls neither, it re-scans the buffer itself (fix.diff:129-143).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: allow_tags tag value: a variant where decode_tag accepted a non-array (bare scalar) payload after '("Tag")' would let a chunk-dependent number hide behind a '(' first byte that incr_starts_bare_scalar does not flag.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: decode_tag already recurses into decode_sv for non-'[' values (XS.xs:4800-4805); relaxing the array-only rule for THAW args is a plausible feature change, and the incr scanner never interrupts on ')' at nest 0 (XS.xs:5350-5352).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an extra non-self-delimiting top-level atom (e.g. relaxed Infinity/NaN or a bare word under allow_unknown) added to decode_sv without updating the incr predicate.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: decode_sv's dispatch and the fix's predicate are separate lists (fix.diff:141-142); a maintainer adding a relaxed literal would touch only decode_sv.

O9_family: parser differential / interpretation conflict (CWE-436): incremental vs one-shot decode disagree on the extent of a top-level scalar

O10_build.toolchain: perl 5 with a C compiler; perl Makefile.PL && make && make test (ExtUtils::MakeMaker)
O10_build.project_tests: t/19_incr.t (incremental parser; fix appends 3 cases), t/116_incr_parse_fixed.t

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Clear F_ALLOW_NONREF (or reject any json_nonref result) inside incr_parse, which also rejects top-level strings and ignores an explicit allow_nonref.

out_of_scope_notes: allow_tags: '("T") [1]' with whitespace after ')' interrupts the incr scanner at nest 0 (XS.xs:5314-5322), so chunking flips success/error rather than the value; not pursued.

Incr WS mode skips bytes with the sign bit set as whitespace on signed-char platforms (XS.xs:5185-5201) while decode_ws stops on them (XS.xs:3281-3282); yields an error, not a value change; not pursued.
Incr comment mode ends only at '\n' (XS.xs:5228) while decode_comment also ends at '\r' (XS.xs:3256); not pursued.
